before: Its -$3, moves to Chase Total Checking.
after: It’s overdrawn by $3.30. Closing it takes $3.30 from Chase Total Checking to clear it.
why: The before was found on the missed-plan save: a negative figure as a thing that moves, in whole dollars. Closing an overdrawn savings account posts the shortfall from the current account (`closeSavings`), so it says that, to the cent.
verified: tests/language-money.test.ts: the sentence, then Close It pressed takes exactly $3.30 from checking

before: Its $1,235, moves to Chase Total Checking.
after: Closing it moves its $1,234.56 to Chase Total Checking.
why: Positive variant: the action first, and the exact figure, not the whole-dollar rounding

before: Its $0, moves to Chase Total Checking.
after: It’s empty, so closing it moves nothing.
why: Zero variant: nothing moves, so it doesn’t say something does

before: Notice given: it closes December 1, 2026.
after: Notice given. It closes December 1, 2026.

after: $15.00 a month, waived in any month you have $500 of electronic deposits (wages, benefits or a tax refund) paid in, or keep $1,500 in it all month, or keep an average of $5,000 across your accounts at the bank. It isn’t waived this month so far. Unless one of those conditions is met, it’s due March 31, 2027.

after: It’s waived this month so far, with $600 paid in.

after: Between your own accounts. Within one bank it’s instant. To another bank it takes as long as the sending bank takes, and abroad it also costs the exchange and the fees.

before: Pays 0.01% a year (0.01% APY). It builds each day and is paid on the last day of the month.
after: Pays 0.01% a year (0.01% APY). Interest builds up daily and is paid on the last day of the month.

why: The engine waives the fee by the shortfall (`short < ifShortAtLeast`, systems/lending.ts), not the payment's size: the before said the wrong condition
